subject: Create Density Surface from Location Data

messages.author: 0d2a4151de2c5ae2
messages.subject: Create Density Surface from Location Data
parts:
Hi all,

I'm working on designing a distance sampling survey. The animal population in this area has been surveyed using other methods for many years but we hope that migrating to a distance sampling approach will save resources. 

Due to the historical sampling of this population I have interesting data that could be helpful for the design phase of the project. One year, an extensive study was executed in which the entire area was surveyed with replication and the GPS location of the observed animals was collected. I am hoping to use the location data of the animals to create a density surface that will inform the simulation of different survey designs.

I want to simulate survey designs using the dsims package with my custom density surface derived from the animal location data stored in a shapefile. The functions in the dsims package require specific object types which I have had trouble replicating. Can anyone tell me how I can create a density grid that is compatible the dsims package? I'm sure someone has done something similar before...

Thank you very much.

Simone

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: {Suspected Spam} [distance-sampling] Create Density Surface from Location Data
parts:
Greetings Simone

There is an argument fitted.model​ in the function make.density​ in the dsims​ package. The documentation for make.density​ describes that argument as taking:

gam object created using mgcv​ with only x and y as explanatory covariates.

That should take you to the mgcv​ package documentation to describe the use of the function gam​ using x- and y- coordinates from your GPS animal locations as predictors.

There is lots of sophistication associated with the gam​ function, but for your purposes, I would suspect you can fit a relatively simple model to generate an object you can feed into make.density​.

Here is a crude example of gam​ at work, first generating simulated data using gamSim​

library(mgcv)
set.seed(2) ## simulate some data...
dat <- gamSim(1,n=400,dist="normal",scale=2)
b <- gam(y~s(x0)+s(x1),data=dat)
class(b)
summary(b)
plot(b,pages=1,residuals=TRUE)
vis.gam(b)

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: Create Density Surface from Location Data
parts:
Dear Simone,

Eric is correct you can pass in an mgcv gam object and as he said it can only contain x and y as the explanatory covariates.

You can also create a density object and if you have a look inside (see code below) you will find an sf object with x and y coordinates and density and strata columns. You can manually extract those coordinates, make predictions, then put the new density values back into the density object if you wanted to predict from a more complicated model with other covariates. Just be careful to keep the data in the same order so the new densities match up with the correct coordinates.

density <- make.density() # Make a density grid specific to your region this is just a basic example

den...@density.surface[[1]]
Simple feature collection with 2500 features and 4 fields
Geometry type: POLYGON
Dimension:     XY
Bounding box:  xmin: 0 ymin: 0 xmax: 2000 ymax: 500
CRS:           NA
First 10 features:
   strata density   x  y                       geometry
1  region       1  10 10 POLYGON ((0 0, 0 20, 20 20,...
2  region       1  30 10 POLYGON ((20 0, 20 20, 40 2...
3  region       1  50 10 POLYGON ((40 0, 40 20, 60 2...
4  region       1  70 10 POLYGON ((60 0, 60 20, 80 2...

coords <- sf::st_drop_geometry(den...@density.surface[[1]][,c("x", "y")])

head(coords)
    x  y
1  10 10
2  30 10
3  50 10
4  70 10
5  90 10
6 110 10
# Do your own predictions using these x and y coordinates and any other covariates you want to add to this prediction data 

new.densities <- rep(2, nrow(coords)) # I shall just replace with values of 2 to show how to put them back in

den...@density.surface[[1]]$density <- new.densities

den...@density.surface[[1]]
Simple feature collection with 2500 features and 4 fields
Geometry type: POLYGON
Dimension:     XY
Bounding box:  xmin: 0 ymin: 0 xmax: 2000 ymax: 500
CRS:           NA
First 10 features:
   strata density   x  y                       geometry
1  region       2  10 10 POLYGON ((0 0, 0 20, 20 20,...
2  region       2  30 10 POLYGON ((20 0, 20 20, 40 2...
3  region       2  50 10 POLYGON ((40 0, 40 20, 60 2...


Best wishes,
Laura
